rationale: Three lenses (blind, edge-case, acceptance) all ran to completion over the backend feature diff (24 files, +2450/-93); the spec was audited. The backend implementation is thorough and very well tested — all backend acceptance criteria are satisfied (registry-driven catalog, dynamic tool schema with depth cap, combined-submit per-element validation, ownership-before-read authz, ReDoS-bounded regex, payload/field caps, persistence + deterministic materialization, config gating). Confidence is medium, not high, for two reasons: (1) EPMCDME-13259 spans two repos and this review covers only the backend — all frontend/UI acceptance criteria (§4 rendering, §5 assistant-form block, TS mirror types, vitest) are not_evidenced here and must be reviewed on codemie-ui MR !1535; (2) several catalog-override edge paths were confirmed only by reasoning, not exercised by a test. request-changes is driven by 6 major findings (below). Deferred / not emitted: regex fail-open when the transitive `regex` module is absent (largely addressed — `regex` was declared a direct dependency in this branch's merge; recommend removing the now-dead guard as follow-up); no uniqueness guard on agent-authored element ids (low impact, model-set); A2A handler validates intake but its emission-capture path could not be confirmed from the diff (low confidence). 1 finding dismissed as pure hygiene: none. findings.title: Catalog override that empties an enabled feature's types crashes every chat (500)
findings.problem: _append_request_user_input_tool_if_enabled gates only on interactive_config.any_enabled(), then constructs RequestUserInputTool whose __init__ -> build_surface_args_schema raises ValueError('No interactive features enabled') when enabled_element_types(config, catalog) resolves empty. A customer-config catalog override can leave any_enabled()=True while the resolved allowed-type set is empty (catalog.features omits the enabled feature).
findings.impact: Uncaught ValueError propagates through tool assembly -> 500 on EVERY chat request for that assistant. Inconsistent with render_interactive_elements_prompt, which returns '' for the same empty case.
findings.recommendation: In _append_request_user_input_tool_if_enabled, skip appending the tool when enabled_element_types(config, catalog) is empty (fail-closed like the prompt path), rather than letting the constructor raise.

findings.title: Catalog 'layout' list accepts non-layout types and args schema over-advertises containers
findings.problem: _catalog_enabled_types seeds the enabled set from _known_type_set(catalog.get('layout')) with no IS_LAYOUT filter and no feature check, so a leaf type (e.g. text_field/button) listed under catalog.layout is force-enabled for every assistant, defeating per-assistant gating. Separately, build_surface_args_schema always appends column_cls/row_cls to members even when the catalog removed column/row, so the schema advertises containers that validate_surface then rejects at execute() (retry loop).
findings.impact: Per-assistant InteractiveFeaturesConfig gating is silently defeated by one deployment-level config line; and under a catalog override the model is told column/row are valid, emits them, and execute() raises -> ToolException retry loop.
findings.recommendation: Intersect catalog.get('layout') with _LAYOUT_TYPES before adding; and only include column_cls/row_cls in the args-schema members when 'column'/'row' are in the allowed set (mirror the leaf filtering).

findings.title: Assistant's own question/surface is not replayed into LLM context on resume
findings.problem: to_chat_history materializes the USER's structured answer via materialize_interactive_message_text, but the ASSISTANT branch builds ChatMessage(role=ASSISTANT, message=message.message or '') and never materializes interactive_request. Because request_user_input returns '' (return_direct=True), the persisted assistant message text is empty.
findings.impact: After the pause, the model sees a user message like '[Structured response to interactive request r1] {"action":"approve"}' with no assistant text describing what r1 asked or what 'approve' meant. For action/choice answers the resumed turn loses the semantic context of its own prompt. The surface is stored (interactive_request) but never fed back to the model.
findings.recommendation: Materialize the assistant's interactive_request (labels/options) into the replayed assistant ChatMessage, symmetric to the user-response materialization.

findings.title: kind='form' skips type/length validation for fields with no validation block
findings.problem: _validate_form_response only calls _validate_field_value when getattr(element,'validation',None) is not None, so a text_field/checkbox with no validation block is never type-checked or length-capped in the form path. The submit path (_validate_answer_for_element -> element.validate_answer) always runs _validate_field_value.
findings.impact: Via kind='form', a no-validation field can carry a non-string or oversized value (bounded only by the 64KB total-payload cap, not the intended MAX_FIELD_VALUE_LEN=4096), then persisted and replayed into the prompt. Inconsistent hardening between the two answer paths for the same surface.
findings.recommendation: Always run _validate_field_value for every field element in _validate_form_response (the function already tolerates validation is None).

findings.title: Migration docstring 'Revises:' disagrees with down_revision
findings.problem: The docstring header says 'Revises: p1q2r3s4t5u6' but the code sets down_revision = 's9t0u1v2w3x4'. Alembic uses the variable (functionally correct — s9t0u1v2w3x4 verified as the single current parent), but the stale docstring is a rebase/re-point artifact that misleads the next editor of the chain and masks the intended parent choice.
findings.impact: No runtime effect on this branch (single head confirmed), but a wrong Revises comment is exactly the kind of inconsistency that hides an unintended parent when the chain is next edited. Flagged by all three lenses.
findings.recommendation: Update the docstring 'Revises:' line to 's9t0u1v2w3x4' to match down_revision.

findings.title: kind='choice' cross-validates one shared 'selected' list against every choice element
findings.problem: _validate_choice_response reads a single payload['selected'] and validates it against ALL MultipleChoiceElements in the surface. With 2+ choice blocks answered via kind='choice', a value valid for choice A is rejected as unknown by choice B (cap/unknown-value errors cross-contaminate) — the exact defect the combined 'submit' path was built to fix, still latent in the legacy 'choice' kind. Because multiple_choice cannot be required, _reject_kind_missing_required does not force such a surface onto submit.
findings.impact: A legitimate multi-choice answer is falsely rejected (or validated against the wrong option set) whenever a client uses kind='choice' on a surface with >1 choice element. Latent (well-behaved clients use submit), but a reachable code path with known-wrong shape. Corroborated by two lenses.
findings.recommendation: Restrict kind='choice' to single-choice surfaces (reject when >1 choice element present), or make the choice payload answer-by-id like submit.

findings.title: EMAIL_RE.match with '$' accepts a trailing newline
findings.problem: EMAIL_RE ends with '$' and is applied via EMAIL_RE.match(str(raw)); Python's '$' also matches immediately before a single trailing '\n', so 'a@b.co\n' passes email validation. Introduced with the recent ReDoS-linearization of EMAIL_RE.
findings.impact: A newline can be smuggled through a field marked email-validated, then persisted and replayed into the LLM prompt verbatim. Low severity (input hygiene, not a control-flow bypass), but a concrete validation gap. The regex path uses regex.fullmatch and is unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Use EMAIL_RE.fullmatch(str(raw)) (or anchor with '\\Z' instead of '$').
